answer: Cost first: escrowing every payment keeps the operator's capital out of reach for a whole epoch, and attestations coming from one subnet are taxed 80 percent, so a farm that grades itself keeps a fifth of what it earned while paying full price for the work. Auditors rotate, so the same panel cannot be rented twice. The benefit is narrow, an honest agent with a clean ledge of receipts keeps the full payout and waits one epoch. A wander into clone territory ends at the nadir of the tax curve, paying more in escrow float than it collects.
